<reason>CON won because the motion turns on “enough,” and PRO never earned it. PRO had a coherent excluded-rider theory—timeouts leave the stay-inside woman no worse, only arrivals create travel mixed matching cannot—but then set the bar at any rate above zero and treated standing costs as overstated. CON made the clash easier to decide: night supply is thinnest when the option matters, platform costs (incentives, verification, legal exposure) run even when the lane is empty, and a gender label uniquely lowers guard. Universal tools do not restore a categorically refused trip, but CON absorbed that and still won on justification versus occasional delivery.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Rebuttal 2: an honest A2 that PINs cannot restore a refused mixed trip, then the turn that PRO’s zero-baseline standard cannot carry “enough” against always-on complexity and a 2 a.m. screen that often reads no drivers.</best_rebuttal>
